desc:
Shopify ongoing management starts with a plan, so regular care of your store has a clear shape from day one. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your store, agrees a task list with you, completes the first round of tasks and delivers a written summary.

## What is Shopify ongoing management?

Shopify ongoing management is the regular upkeep of a live store: product edits, app and theme checks, small fixes, order support and reporting. Instead of dealing with each job when it becomes urgent, you hand the routine to a team that follows an agreed list.

This starter plan is the first step. It is a fixed-price sprint that sets up the routine and does the first round of work. The monthly plan that follows is quoted separately.

## Why stores need regular care

A store is never finished. Prices change, products sell out, apps update, themes age and customers find new ways to get stuck. Small problems that nobody owns grow slowly. A broken link stays broken, a banner stays up after the sale, and a product page keeps an old photo.

Owners often fix only what hurts the most, and the rest piles up. A written task list changes that. Each item has a place, an order and a record that it was done.

## How regular management supports results

Steady upkeep keeps the parts of the store that earn money in good condition: product pages, collections, navigation, checkout and email notifications. When those parts stay accurate and fast, shoppers meet fewer reasons to leave. Time matters too. Every hour you spend on small edits is an hour not spent on buying, marketing or customers.

Reports close the loop. A short written summary shows what was done and what the numbers suggest for next month, so decisions rest on what the store actually did. Results still depend on your products, prices and traffic, and we say so plainly.

## What a good starter plan includes

- A review of products, collections, pages, apps, theme and settings.
- A prioritized task list agreed with you before work starts.
- A weekly check list that describes what to look at each week.
- Routine tasks completed in the first sprint, such as product edits and page updates.
- A check of apps and theme for anything outdated or unused.
- Small fixes to links, text, images and settings.
- Order and notification checks to confirm that customers receive the right emails.
- Progress updates, so you are never left guessing.
- A calendar showing what happens in each week.
- A written summary of every change made.

## What we do

We join your store as staff or collaborator and read through it as a customer and as an owner. We then send a task list and ask you to rank what matters most. After you agree, we work through the list in that order and note each change.

The Basic package creates the plan and completes an initial batch of routine tasks. Standard covers a first full month of care, with progress updates and an apps, theme and settings review. Premium adds weekly updates, a short sales report with three actions, and a quarter plan with a quote for monthly care. A routine task is a small, clearly defined job, so large builds and redesigns are quoted separately.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Write your tasks as short, specific requests.
- Rank the list so the most valuable work is done first.
- Tell us about planned sales, launches and supplier changes in advance.
- Approve anything that changes how the store looks or charges customers.
- Read the weekly summary and reply with questions.

**Avoid:**
- Sending a long, vague list with no priorities.
- Making large changes yourself while we work on the same pages.
- Treating the sprint as a replacement for a full redesign.
- Skipping the summary, which is your record of what changed.
- Waiting until a problem costs sales before asking for help.

## Who this is for

This service suits owners who are tired of doing every small job themselves and want a dependable helper for the routine. It suits stores that grew quickly and now have loose ends, and it suits sellers who want to test regular management before agreeing to a monthly plan.

## What we need from you

We need a staff or collaborator invitation to your Shopify store, a short list of what you want done and the names of any apps you rely on. We never need your password. You own all the work in your own store from day one. Send tasks by email or message after you order, and we confirm the process in a short checklist.
